audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows contradicted their own explanation: whys[0] 'Level 1 is yours' under a row labelled Darius rated 2/10, whys[1] 'Level 2 is skill' under Darius, whys[3] 'Levels 4-5 are even' under Darius, whys[4] 'Level 6 is yours' under Skill.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Warwick, Skill, Warwick, Skill, Warwick, Darius, Darius and the whys track it; the mirror (darius__warwick) then settles the one row they differ on — Level 3 is Darius, Level 6 is Warwick.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Warwick, Skill, Darius, Skill, Warwick, Darius, Darius in both layers as one atomic group, ratings re-keyed; whys[2] rewritten to Darius' side to match the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is called 'matchup-defining' everywhere but its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 — the longest cooldown in the early lane and the entire reason a step-up is safe or not. Infinite Duress is 110s and suppresses for 1.5s.
audit.corrected: 26s Apprehend written into spikes[1] and wants.you[1]; the 1.5s suppression into whys[4], mid and spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Infinite Duress hard-counters his Apprehend pull and Noxian Guillotine' and 'cancels his Apprehend and Guillotine outright' assert an interrupt interaction Riot's text does not describe — the mirror removed the same claim in the other direction for exactly this reason. Also the standard 'Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter'.
audit.why: Whether Apprehend interrupts the leap, or the leap cancels a Guillotine already in flight, is not in the kit data and needsResearch is empty. What IS true and stronger: the suppression lasts 1.5 seconds and a suppressed champion casts nothing — so the play is to leap after Apprehend is spent, not to race it.
audit.corrected: The interrupt claim replaced with the verifiable suppression duration and the Apprehend-spent timing, in spikes[1], whys[4], mid and wants.you[1]; R restated as a directional collision leap.

edits.after: Infinite Duress suppresses for 1.5s, and a suppressed Darius casts nothing — leap once Apprehend is spent, 26s at rank 1, and burst before Decimate's blade heals him back.

edits.after: Leap in after Apprehend is spent — 26s down at rank 1

edits.before: Level 3-6 is your window: dodge Decimate, dash in with Blood Hunt, and Jaws-heal through his early bleed on the return. At 6 your Infinite Duress cancels his Apprehend and Guillotine outright, letting you burst him before five stacks accrue.
edits.after: Level 3 is his once Apprehend is online, 4-5 even out, and 6 is yours: Infinite Duress suppresses for 1.5s and he casts nothing through it — burst him before Hemorrhage reaches five stacks and his enrage attack damage switches on.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Darius's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a directional leap that suppresses for 1.5s — he casts nothing inside it. Noxian Guillotine refreshes on a kill, so never fight it low.

notes: Chart rebuilt from the packet with the mirror's two corrections applied (Level 3 to Darius, Level 6 to Warwick). Removed an unverifiable interrupt claim that appeared three times — that Infinite Duress cancels Apprehend and Noxian Guillotine. Riot's text does not describe it and the mirror deliberately removed the same claim from the other side, so I replaced it with what is verifiable and actually more useful: the suppression is 1.5s, a suppressed champion casts nothing, and Apprehend is 26s at rank 1. The packet suspect 'Your Infinite Duress' is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct name with a leading possessive.
